papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: The study characterized vigilance-state transitions in mice using EEG/EMG recordings and machine learning, finding that NREMS-to-REMS transitions are longest while REMS-to-NREMS are shortest. SVM classifiers trained on stable-state features predicted expert-defined transition midpoints, providing a reproducible framework for quantifying transitions.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: Using a 34-hour sleep deprivation study with fMRI/EEG and NIRS, the authors found that CSF low-frequency oscillations increase with time awake and peak in the early morning, and are associated with vigilance and reticular activating system activity but not plasma norepinephrine. These findings indicate that time awake and diurnal time independently modulate vasomotion.

papers.title: ICA-S3M: switching state-space model guided automatic EEG artifact removal from independent components.
papers.summary: The paper introduces ICA-S3M, a two-stage pipeline combining ICA with a switching state-space model to remove EMG artifacts from EEG. It outperforms a CNN on simulated and semi-synthetic datasets, reducing RRMSE from 0.83 to 0.23 and improving SNR by 12.4 dB, while avoiding spurious alpha oscillations.

papers.title: Rapid associative spine enlargement is required for cognitive function and stable wakefulness
papers.summary: The study developed SynC, a chemogenetic perturbation that selectively blocks associative spine enlargement, and found that acute inhibition in mice impaired cognitive behaviors and reduced cortical spike correlations during quiet wakefulness. These effects recovered within an hour, demonstrating that rapid associative spine enlargement is required for stable wakefulness and cognition.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: In non-human primates with MPTP-induced parkinsonism, beta oscillations and motor impairments were enhanced during wakefulness and NREM sleep but attenuated during REM sleep, with beta suppression preceding REM onset. This shows that Parkinsonian network dysfunction is dynamically gated by brain state, and REM sleep disengages beta oscillations to permit rapid movements.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: The authors analyzed automatically detected sleep spindles in dogs for compliance with three face validity criteria from human EEG: short duration, midline distribution of fast spindles, and amplitude-chirp association. All three criteria were observed in most datasets, supporting the validity of the detection method and the dog as a model for sleep spindle research.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: This study proposed a dual-domain framework for automated EEG-based ASD classification, combining time-frequency analysis with Horizontal Visibility Graph (HVG) network modeling. The DWT-HVG framework with a Soft Voting Ensemble achieved an accuracy of 93.54% and an AUC of 98.17% using stratified 10-fold cross-validation, demonstrating an accurate and computationally efficient screening approach.

papers.title: PVT inhibition mitigates neuropathology and cognitive deficits in chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
papers.summary: Using whole-brain immediate-early gene imaging in a mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, the study identifies the paraventricular thalamus (PVT) as a persistently hyperactive hub. Chemogenetic inhibition of PVT attenuates neuronal damage and improves cognitive and sleep outcomes.

papers.title: Environmental context outweighs early methamphetamine exposure in shaping behavioral and glutamatergic outcomes in rats.
papers.summary: This study in rats shows that environmental conditions (enrichment, housing) have a stronger influence on behavioral and glutamatergic outcomes than early methamphetamine exposure. Effects were task- and context-dependent, with enriched pre-weaning conditions increasing striatal and decreasing hippocampal glutamate.

papers.title: Chronic corticosterone exposure disrupts bile acids homeostasis associated with circadian dysfunction in the liver of chickens.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of chronic corticosterone exposure on hepatic bile acid metabolism and circadian clock in chickens, finding disrupted rhythms and altered bile acid levels. Glucocorticoids were shown to enhance MRP2-mediated apical bile acid efflux, linking stress to enterohepatic bile acid remodeling.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: This study analyzed brain-heart interactions during controlled breathing and found respiratory-phase-dependent differences, with inhale-hold associated with increased gamma power, higher recurrence rate, and elevated heart rate compared to exhale-hold. The findings suggest respiration modulates the organization of brain-body dynamics, supporting its role in dynamically tuning brain-heart interactions.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function: Review of the literature findings, methodology, and interpretation.
papers.summary: This review examines the DTI-ALPS technique as a non-invasive MRI marker of glymphatic system function, summarizing findings from 393 articles. It concludes that DTI-ALPS is highly sensitive but non-specific, reflecting white matter microstructural damage and neuroinflammation, with potential for large-scale clinical screening.

papers.title: Single-channel gamma burst dynamics and adaptive deep learning for robust EEG motor state decoding.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a compact EEG decoding framework using gamma burst dynamics and adaptive deep learning for motor state classification from a single channel. It improves cross-session accuracy by over 10% compared to non-adaptive baselines on the WAY-EEG-GAL dataset.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: This study introduces AXELLSTM, an EEG-based fatigue detection framework combining interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling. Using nested LOSO validation, it identified stable fatigue-related features and channels, achieving a Macro-F1 of 0.7143 with a lightweight model, demonstrating a favorable balance between performance and complexity.

papers.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed parent and child acceptability and preference of home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) versus in-lab polysomnography (PSG) in children. HSAT was feasible and preferred by 60% of parents but only 33% of children, with frequent sensor adjustments needed, especially nasal cannula and pulse oximeter.

papers.title: Chronotype, temporal eating patterns, and sleep behaviors among physically active university students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 200 physically active university students, later first and last caloric intake independently predicted lower Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire scores, explaining 51.1% of variance. Evening chronotype was associated with poorer sleep behaviors and sleep quality.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: This study exposed young adult rats to 1 week of chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) and found increased FosB expression in trigeminal premotor regions and enhanced noradrenergic innervation of the trigeminal motor nucleus, along with selectively increased digastric muscle activity during arousal from sleep, without altering sleep architecture. The results suggest CIH induces plasticity in trigeminal circuits that enhances arousal-related jaw-opening muscle responsiveness.

papers.title: AI-assisted identification and in vitro validation of a MyD88 pathway modulator for inflammatory airway signalling.
papers.summary: This study used AI-assisted de novo ligand design and optimization to identify a MyD88 pathway modulator, then validated it in vitro. The compound reduced ROS levels, downregulated TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling components, and decreased pro-inflammatory and Th2 cytokines in epithelial, macrophage, and mast cell models.

papers.title: White matter hyperintensity drives EEG microstate abnormalities in arteriosclerotic cerebral small vessel disease.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study analyzed EEG microstates in patients with white matter hyperintensity (WMH) with and without dementia and healthy controls. WMH patients showed altered microstate features, particularly reduced microstate C temporal parameters, which correlated with WMH burden and cognitive scores, and SVM/LR models distinguished groups with up to 79% accuracy.

papers.title: CEREBROVASCULAR EVENTS AND NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS WITH ALTERATIONS IN POLYSOMNOGRAPHIC INDICATORS FOLLOWING CARDIAC SURGERY.
papers.summary: The prospective study of 104 cardiac surgery patients found postoperative polysomnographic alterations (increased sleep latency, arousal index) correlated with neurocognitive impairment, and citicoline administration improved MoCA scores and sleep stabilization by day 30.

papers.title: Associations of Plasma Total Tau Level and MMSE Score With Polysomnographic Data in Middle-Aged Men With Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In middle-aged men with severe obstructive sleep apnea, plasma total tau levels correlated negatively with deep sleep duration and oxygen saturation, and positively with apnea-hypopnea index and oxygen desaturation index, while MMSE scores correlated negatively with these sleep disruption measures.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: In patients with atrial fibrillation, resting-state EEG revealed reduced alpha-band functional connectivity associated with cognitive impairment; alpha-band wPLI was independently associated with cognitive status and showed potential as a biomarker.

papers.title: Nocturnal heart rate variability in Parkinson's disease: associations with autonomic dysfunction, cognitive function, and mood symptoms.
papers.summary: This study compared nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV) derived from polysomnography between Parkinson's disease (PD) patients and healthy controls, and examined associations with non-motor symptoms. PD patients showed reduced sympathetic influence on HRV during sleep, and stronger parasympathetic influence correlated with better cognitive performance.

papers.title: Adverse experiences in childhood and adolescence in relation to sleep health in adulthood: An overview of systematic reviews and a global evidence map.
authors: World Sleep Society Global Adolescent Sleep Project Taskforce
papers.summary: This overview of systematic reviews synthesized evidence on associations between adverse childhood and adolescent experiences (ACA) and adult sleep health. ACA exposure was consistently associated with poorer sleep, but overall certainty was low due to critically low confidence and high risk of bias, with evidence concentrated in the Americas and Europe.

papers.title: Association Between Nocturnal Oxygen Desaturation and the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study examined associations between the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and nocturnal oxygenation parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). AHI was positively associated with oxygen desaturation index and T90, and inversely associated with minimum and mean nocturnal SpO2, with all Holm-adjusted p-values <0.001.

papers.title: Negative BOLD response to interictal discharges in epilepsy using intracranial EEG-fMRI.
authors: the, Calgary Comprehensive Epilepsy Program collaborators
papers.summary: This study compared positive and negative BOLD responses to interictal epileptiform discharges in intracranial EEG-fMRI. Positive BOLD clusters were significantly closer to epileptogenic tissue than negative clusters, and negative clusters showed greater spatial overlap with the default mode network, suggesting they may reflect network deactivation.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves neurocognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation: an experimental study based on hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: This experimental study investigated whether electro-nape-acupuncture (ENA) at bilateral Fengchi and Gongxue acupoints improves cognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) in male Wistar rats. ENA improved spatial learning and memory and recognition memory, and reversed CSD-induced decreases in hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyrus.

papers.title: Association between habitual sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease: A cross-sectional study based on NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study using NHANES data (2007-2018) found a significant positive correlation between longer habitual sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease prevalence, which persisted after adjustment. The study advocates incorporating body composition into AD risk assessment based on sleep time's predictive value.

papers.title: Adolescent depression recognition and symptom prediction based on multi-view EEG network: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study developed a Multi-view Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (MVA-GCN) based on resting-state EEG to recognize adolescent depression. MVA-GCN achieved 99.84% accuracy in the present dataset compared to 86.43% for questionnaire-based machine learning models, and identified gamma-band functional connectivity and alpha-band power as potential electrophysiological correlates.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations between sleepiness and sleep disturbances across pregnancy.
papers.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study of 3286 pregnant women found that sleepiness followed a U-shaped trajectory across pregnancy and was consistently associated with insomnia, short sleep duration, sleep loss, and snoring from midpregnancy onward. The findings suggest screening for sleep disturbances in pregnant women reporting sleepiness.

papers.title: From bench to bedside: current evidence and prospects for acupuncture in managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on acupuncture for perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), proposing that risk factors interact through shared pathways and that acupuncture, via the gut-brain axis, modulates gut microbiota, neural circuits, and synaptic homeostasis to reduce PND incidence. It concludes that electroacupuncture and transcutaneous acupoint stimulation construct a coordinated neuroprotective network.

papers.title: Armillariella tabescens polysaccharide targets microglial glycolysis to alleviate sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation through the mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.summary: This study isolated a polysaccharide (ATEP) from Armillariella tabescens and showed that it alleviates sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation by inhibiting mTOR signaling, correcting glycolytic shift, and promoting microglial M2 polarization in a mouse model and BV2 cells. The findings highlight ATEP as a natural candidate for neuroprotection.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Insomnia, Social Dysfunction, Suicidality, and Depressive Symptoms in Rural Adults with Schizophrenia: A Sex-Stratified Analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 931 rural adults with schizophrenia found that insomnia, social dysfunction, and suicidality were associated with depressive symptoms, with insomnia directly linked and indirect effects via social dysfunction and suicidality. Women reported higher symptom scores, but sex did not moderate the associations.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared heart rate variability (HRV) among seizure patients with and without interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and a non-seizure group, finding lower vagally mediated HRV in seizure patients. IEDs were not associated with additional resting autonomic alterations.

papers.title: Digital screen exposure and migraine burden: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the association between digital screen exposure and migraine/headache burden across 22 studies (N=14,763). Higher screen exposure was associated with 60% greater odds of migraine/headache (pooled OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.38–1.86), with low certainty evidence and proposed mechanisms including blue light and circadian disruption.

papers.title: Associations of sleep duration variability and depressive symptoms with gastrointestinal disease among middle-aged and older adults: A cohort study.
papers.summary: This cohort study using CHARLS and HRS data found that greater sleep duration variability was associated with increased risk of gastrointestinal disease in middle-aged and older adults, with depressive symptoms partially mediating this association.

papers.title: Association between the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index and obstructive sleep apnea risk: Mediating role of body mass index in U.S. adults.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 4,564 U.S. adults found that a higher C-reactive protein–triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) was independently associated with increased obstructive sleep apnea risk, with each unit increase linked to 43% higher odds. BMI mediated 56.3% of the association.

papers.title: Teaching-research conflict and self-reported strain in early academic careers: Selective role investment among postdoctoral teacher-researchers.
papers.summary: This qualitative study of 30 postdoctoral researchers in Chinese higher education found that teaching-research conflict led to selective role investment, such as protecting writing time and compressing teaching preparation. These strategies supported short-term career viability but were accompanied by fatigue and ethical discomfort.

papers.title: Single-Site ALK-Positive Histiocytosis With TFG-ALK Fusion: Expanding the Clinical Spectrum of This Rare Entity.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.summary: This case report presents the first instance of single-site ALK-positive histiocytosis with a TFG-ALK fusion in a pulmonary nodule, which was treated by resection alone with no recurrence. It expands the clinical spectrum, suggesting this fusion can be associated with localized indolent disease.

papers.title: (Cost-)effectiveness of a combined lifestyle intervention integrated into standard care for low back pain compared to usual care for people with persistent non-specific low back pain who are overweight or obese: Protocol for a randomised controlled trial with parallel economic and process evaluations (Back2Health).
papers.summary: This protocol describes a two-armed randomised controlled trial (Back2Health) evaluating the (cost-)effectiveness of a combined lifestyle intervention integrated into standard care versus usual care for persistent non-specific low back pain in overweight or obese adults. Co-primary outcomes are physical functioning and physical activity over 36 months.
